This is "State" and not "Inventory".   Please move the file accordingly.

The reason is that we want to limit signals emitted from the Inventory interfaces.

> The reason is that we want to limit signals emitted from the Inventory interfaces.

Can you explain a bit more on this ?

Patrick, I have updated to move from Inventory to state. 
There is still a pending question from Manoj.
Acknowledged
Can I get a reference here to where a proposed implementation of this is?

ReadyToRemove was added to Redfish in 2025.3 for the BMC, Redfish assembly, and Redfish Chassis (It was already in Drive and PCIeDevice)
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/84402/2/redfish-core/schema/dmtf/csdl/Manager_v1.xml

IBM plans to use ReadyToRemove for redundant BMCs with the backend implemented most likely in the proposed BMC App  
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/70233

This ReadyToRemove is part of IBM's Concurrent maintenance 

I do know ReadyToRemove is used by other Redfish implementations today on PCIeDevice and Drive, although I haven't seen anything in Redfish 
https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Aopenbmc%2Fbmcweb%20ReadyToRemove&type=code
https://github.com/ODIM-Project/ODIM/blob/81c02da794c25446817e363da87956d18b0c28dd/lib-dmtf/model/storage.go#L201
Done
Done

The way this reads, something in the system would prepare the FRU to be removed and then set this to true.  Is that what the flow is?

I thought it was that a Redfish request will come in to ask that a FRU be prepared for removal, and bmcweb would set this and other code would watch it and prepare it.

I could just be overthinking it.
The description I used is similar to the description in the Redfish property description of ReadyToRemove in the Redfish Property Guide

ok, yea I see this in a PCIe schema at https://www.dmtf.org/sites/default/files/standards/documents/DSP0268_2023.1.html:


> Setting the value to true shall cause the service to perform appropriate actions to quiesce the device. A task may spawn while the device is quiescing.

Though most of the redfish descriptions have the same thing you have.

Maybe could you update the wording to say something similar (e.g. setting it to true will...)?

The version 1.10+ description of ReadyToRemove doesn't have the extra information. The version 1.7+ has the extra information about setting...
1.10+ is a more recent version, so should I go with 1.10+
Acknowledged
Can you add a link to Redfish? maybe list the Redfish resources it is at? Can you mentioned this is needed for an operation like Concurrent maintenance ?
I have updated.
Done
Done
I would still prefer an update that it can also be used to tell the system to prepare for it.
I have updated
Done
Does this interface require other (inventory?) interfaces to be implemented by the object?

Theree are apps that will be invoked when ReadyToRemove is set to true and false, respectively which are supposed to handle the inventory updates associated with the Concurrent Maintenance process. The details of this have not been completely flushed out.

> Does this interface require other (inventory?) interfaces to be implemented by the object?

If you want this for your BMC, you would implement inventory.item.bmc for example.
Done

I find this a bit confusing. Does setting this to true imply the item has been quiesced and ready to be removed, or, setting this to true kicks off the quisce process? This and the previous statement seem a bit contradictory.
Setting ReadyToRemove to "True"  kicks off the quiesce process and conversely setting it to "False" begins the process of resuming activity to the part that was just replaced.
Acknowledged
Does there need to be a default value?
I have added the default value of false
Done
Should the value persist across system/bmc reboots, once a user has set it?
If the active BMC reboots then the value would not persist: the user would need to redo the Concurrent Maintenance operation.
I thought it would persist until an app or client changes it?? Same as other state properties. Although, booting the system / rebooting the bmc during an operation like this, seems odd.
Acknowledged
How do we know what item this is? Does this need to have associations to other object(s) or other expectations (path/service) documented here?

There are apps that will be invoked when ReadyToRemove is set to true 
and false, respectively which are supposed to handle the inventory 
updates associated with the Concurrent Maintenance process. The details 
of this have not been completely flushed out.
Acknowledged
This interface should be implemented on the inventory item that uses this.
Should we update what Gunnar said above in the description?
Done
If the quiesce fails, what is the property expected to hold? How are errors communicated?

The Concurrent Maintenance will take the appropriate actions. The details
of this have not been completely flushed out.
Acknowledged

Its odd that redfish specification choose a boolean to do this rather an action. But since this is already supported in redfish , the proposed dbus mapping seems reasonable to me.

As per Redfish spec, a PATCH operation can result in either synchronous or asynchronous responses. Although this is a boolean and not an action, it seems like its still valid to return a task back for error propagation.
I don't see details about error handling.
I have added information about error handling.
Done
It's not very clear if this is State or Control. At the moment it's in the State namespace but offers Control.
It is a State and the setting of this to true or false will cause the service to perform appropriate actions related to an item.
Acknowledged
What is the expectation post removal? The object implementing this is deleted?
Yes, in the case of ReadyToRemove set to true and item is removed.
Acknowledged

The expectation post removal, might be a state of Present = False 

https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Inventory/Item.interface.yaml#L14
Don't see details either way (value set to false or object removed) documented.
I have added some details about what happens when value is set to false or when object is removed.
Done
Please add those errors here (look at other interfaces that throw errors on property access).
This would be implementation dependent.Is it a good idea to add, NotAllowed, NotPresent?
I think it'd be fine to add the ones you plan on using.
I have added errors

Why did you (1) markdown escape a link to the (2) entire Redfish specification?

1. Don't markdown escape things you want formatted as markdown.
2. Link to specific schema files (ie. JSON or XML) you are referring to.  Nobody wants to try to search through a thousand page PDF for whatever you are referencing.
Specification link has been removed. Schema file link added.
Done

It seems like this is intended to be part of an Inventory object, but we should not "attach" state to objects in the /xyz/openbmc_project/inventory namespace.  I want to limit signals from there to actual inventory changes.

I think you need to document more how this is supposed to be used, what is the dbus URIs you expect this to live under (we have YAML directives for documenting that), what associations you expect to see, etc. before this can be accepted.

I had originally implemented this as part of inventory object, but you had asked https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/83617/comment/0c85f049_5ad94d1f/ for it to be moved to state.

Yes, exactly.  It should be "moved to state".  But that isn't just an Interface naming statement... that is also a "how is this hosted in dbus statement".  That's the part that you've given no words on.

Changing an interface name was the trivial part.  Now you need to do the design work of what moving to the state namespace means from a dbus path perspective.
Association has been added.
Done
We should not be adding InternalFailure on new interfaces.  Your caller has no idea what they can do about this.
InternalFailure removed
Done
